title: Used Car Inspection and Damage Detection
summary: Guided photo capture and damage detection for used-car evaluations, with panel-wise damage maps, odometer and chassis checks and draft refurbishment items for evaluators to confirm.

seo.title: Used Car Inspection and Damage Detection AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI for used-car evaluation: guided photos, panel-wise damage detection, odometer and chassis checks against the RC, and draft refurbishment estimates.

problem.intro: Dealers, used-car platforms and auction houses evaluate cars at customers' homes, exchange desks and procurement yards, usually with a checklist and phone photos. The quality of that evaluation decides the purchase price, the refurbishment bill and whether the next buyer trusts the listing.

pain_points.title: Grading varies by evaluator
pain_points.detail: Experienced and new evaluators grade the same scratch or dent differently, which shows up in procurement prices and listing quality.

pain_points.title: Damage found after purchase
pain_points.detail: A repainted panel or cracked bumper bracket missed at evaluation becomes an unplanned refurbishment cost.

pain_points.title: Disputes over pre-existing damage
pain_points.detail: Without a clear photo record, sellers, buyers and logistics partners argue over when a dent appeared.

pain_points.title: Wrong car, reused photos
pain_points.detail: Photos of a different vehicle, or reused from an earlier listing, slip through when nobody checks the chassis number on the image.

solution.overview: We build a guided inspection flow for your evaluation app. It walks the evaluator or seller through a fixed set of angles and close-ups, checking blur, glare and framing before each photo is accepted. Vision models then segment the car into panels and detect scratches, dents, cracks, rust, misaligned panels and colour or gloss differences that suggest repaint. The odometer and the chassis number are read from photos and compared with the RC details. Each finding is marked on the image with a severity grade and mapped to refurbishment line items from your parts and labour rate card. The evaluator confirms or corrects findings before the report reaches pricing.
capabilities: Guided capture with live checks for blur, glare, distance and framing
Panel-level detection of scratches, dents, cracks, rust and misaligned panels
Colour and gloss mismatch cues that suggest repaint, for confirmation with a paint thickness gauge
Odometer and chassis number reading compared with RC details
Duplicate and reused photo detection across past inspections
Draft refurbishment line items priced from your parts and labour rate card

workflow.title: Guided capture
workflow.detail: The app guides the evaluator through the required exterior, interior, odometer and chassis number photos.

workflow.title: Quality check
workflow.detail: Each photo is checked for blur, glare and framing, and failed shots are retaken on the spot.

workflow.title: Detect and grade damage
workflow.detail: Models detect damage by panel and grade severity on your grading scale.

workflow.title: Check identity
workflow.detail: Odometer and chassis number are read from photos and compared with the RC, and photos are checked for reuse.

workflow.title: Evaluator review
workflow.detail: Low-confidence findings and any RC mismatch go to the evaluator, who confirms or corrects them.

workflow.title: Report and estimate
workflow.detail: The inspection report and draft refurbishment estimate go to the pricing team and the DMS.

inputs: Guided exterior, interior, odometer and chassis number photos
RC details from the document or an authorised vehicle data provider
Paint thickness gauge readings entered by the evaluator
Your grading scale and parts and labour rate card
outputs: Panel-wise damage map with marked images
Image archive linked to the vehicle record
human_in_the_loop: The evaluator confirms damage grades and every identity mismatch before the report is final. Purchase price and offers are set by your pricing team, and structural, flood and engine checks remain physical inspections.
integrations: Used-car pricing tool or auction platform
CRM for seller and buyer records
Cloud storage for the image archive
guardrails: Does not set prices or certify roadworthiness
Asks for a retake rather than grading a poor photo
Every finding marked on the source image
Structural, flood and engine condition left to physical checks
Seller details on RC images access-controlled and masked in logs
compliance_notes: Owner details from RC images are personal data and are handled under the DPDP Act 2023.
Vehicle registration lookups are made only through authorised channels for VAHAN-based data.

pilot.scope: One procurement hub or dealer exchange desk, running the guided flow alongside the current evaluation for hatchbacks, sedans and compact SUVs.
deliverables: Capture guide and grading scale agreed with senior evaluators
Pilot app flow with damage detection
Agreement report against senior evaluator grades

what_we_measure.how: System findings compared with a senior evaluator's grading of the same cars.
Damage found at refurbishment that was not recorded at evaluation, split by what the system and the evaluator each caught.
Share of photos rejected by quality checks, by evaluator.
Time per evaluation with and without the guided flow.

faqs.q: Can it detect accident history or flood damage?
faqs.a: Only visible cues such as panel gaps, repaint signs or rust patterns. Structural damage, flood exposure and engine condition need a physical inspection, and the report says so.

faqs.q: Does it work outdoors and in poor light?
faqs.a: The guided flow checks every photo and asks for a retake when glare, shadow or darkness hides the panel. We tune on photos from your evaluators across different lighting during the pilot.

faqs.q: Can sellers use it for self-inspection?
faqs.a: Yes. The same guided capture can run in a seller-facing app, with an evaluator reviewing findings remotely before any physical visit.

faqs.q: Can it plug into our existing evaluation app?
faqs.a: Yes. The capture guide and models can be added as an SDK or called through an API from your current app, so evaluators keep their familiar tool.
